source_scope.decision_policy: Create or update only when the technique has a concrete SGDK/Mega Drive consequence.

create_new_skill.reason: Multi-point probes, semi-solid platforms, slopes and large-sprite collision are foundational for platformers, beat 'em ups and fighters.
Animated backgrounds and runtime tile changes need VRAM slot ownership and DMA discipline.
Shadow/Highlight and scroll effects are key Mega Drive-native spectacle techniques.
Function-pointer dispatch avoids giant behavior switches and supports enemy catalogs.
Fade, flush and mutex transitions prevent re-entrant scene changes and VRAM/CRAM corruption.
Advanced claims need a single gate that routes work to the required domain skills.
16 Tile-style per-cell palette, priority and flip metadata must become explicit scene data.
Vibrant Mega Drive art depends on CRAM ownership, indexed color and 9-bit quantization.
Large sprites, crowds and bosses fail visually when per-scanline sprite limits are ignored.
Road, water and pseudo-3D effects need explicit HScroll table ownership and camera mapping.
Mid-frame palette changes require timing, CRAM ownership and artifact risk control.
Checkerboard transparency must be reviewed against display/capture assumptions.
Audio streaming and PCM playback require explicit Z80/68000 responsibility boundaries.
Multi-part bosses and characters need anchor, SAT and collision coherence.
CPU-rendered pseudo-3D or polygon-like effects rewrite tiles and need strict cost controls.
Levels need one contract binding camera, art, collision, entities, audio and evidence.
Sprite sheets require hardware-shaped art budgets, palette discipline and frame consistency.
SNES, PC-98, high-color and AI art need controlled conversion into Mega Drive constraints.
SFX assets need FM/PSG/PCM ownership and channel-risk planning.
Visual and runtime claims must map to BlastEm/screenshot/SRAM/VDP evidence.

improve_existing.needed_change: Consume new scroll, DMA, sprite, entity, transition and guardian contracts.
Route art direction through scroll FX, DMA and guardian gates.
Require tilemap attributes, palette conflicts and streaming evidence for advanced backgrounds.
Accept external techniques only through explicit VDP constraints.
Consume sprite-asset-budget-curator for model-sheet fidelity and rejected-sheet prevention.
Consume color-conversion-curator and palette-cram-curator before asset conversion approval.
Add display-mode review for dithering, palette vibrance and CRT/composite assumptions.
Route state transitions, entity dispatch and SGDK 2.11 API claims to new architecture skills.
Review function-pointer entity tables, transition locks and DMA queue misuse.
Expose curation validator and evidence checks in closeout workflows.
Route line-scroll and tilemap attribute claims to dedicated skills.
Route palette, transition, VDP dump and SFX claims to dedicated gates.
Include AAA curation package validation as an optional canonical audit for training cases.
